findings.reason: a control that cannot go red leaves the node's only measure resting on assertions the base revision already satisfies, which is the defect the done-when item exists to catch.
findings.text: s93 declares "Negative control: at the base revision the cold pass loads the history at least 100 times", but at head (fc8e237f) `recovery_stream._lane_reference_rates` is `@lru_cache(maxsize=16)` keyed on (project, window_bucket) and calls `ledger.load` once per key: running `_budget_overrun_cause` 100 times in one tick, and 100 times across 100 s, measured 1 history load each, so the at-most-one-load assertion already passes on the unfixed code and the declared control cannot fire

findings.reason: the repair would be aimed at a per-run rebuild that does not exist, while the measured cost sits in the search for it in buckets or in the size of the single decode.
findings.text: the Why says the reference rates "are rebuilt for every run the sweep classifies", but at the base revision the read is cached per project and five-minute bucket (`@lru_cache(maxsize=16)` at recovery_stream.py:154, keyed `(project, window_bucket)`), so a cold pass of 100 runs costs one load and the 14.6 % of station samples the section attributes to per-run rebuilds cannot come from that mechanism

findings.reason: an implementer cannot satisfy both the fixed-listing bound and the concurrent-visibility assertion, and will either fail the gate or silently widen the bound beyond 3 × 200.
findings.text: s94's Deliverable requires "Every per-run check the sweep makes answers from the listing the sweep already holds", while the done-when's second case requires a pointer "written during the sweep" to be seen by "a check made after the write, as at the base revision"; `open_run_index.read_scope` sets its snapshot to `tuple(runs.list_live())` at scope entry (open_run_index.py:44), so a held listing cannot see a pointer written after it was taken — the two requirements are contradictory

response_events.note: s93's done-when now measures rows decoded across a bucket roll: the base revision decodes the whole seven-day window on every roll, the repair decodes only rows added since the previous bucket; the negative control is that whole-window decode
